title: Add pluggable RAG bridge quickstart and docsite walkthrough
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: provide a compact, opinionated quickstart that demonstrates how to plug third-party indexers and tool adapters into a RAG flow while keeping the same Redwood API and telemetry contracts. This PR adds a developer-friendly local playground, a docsite walkthrough page, and a set of contract tests and telemetry presets so teams can iterate on adapter implementations quickly.

What this includes: 1) quickstart/bridge-playground: a minimal Docker Compose playground that runs: - a local vector indexer (pgvector-backed demo), - a lightweight tool-adapter shim (HTTP adapter with OpenAPI contract), - a Redwood-compatible RAG runner stub that exercises tool-calling and structured outputs; 2) docs/site/walkthroughs/rag-bridge.md: step-by-step guided walkthrough for the docsite with screenshots and interactive code blocks; 3) tests/bridge-contracts: contract tests that validate request/response shapes for the indexer and tool-adapter (used by CI smoke); 4) examples/adapter-templates: two adapter templates (python-fastapi and ts-express) with README on auth, retries, and security practices; 5) telemetry/presets/bridge-presets.yaml: suggested probe configurations and metric names for teams integrating new adapters.

Checklist: - [x] Local playground with reproducible start (docker compose) - [x] Docsite walkthrough with runnable snippets - [x] Contract tests + GitHub Actions smoke job - [x] Adapter templates + developer notes - [x] Telemetry presets and sample dashboards - [x] Line-level README and quick commands for dev loop

Backward compatibility and constraints: the quickstart uses Redwood public API surface only; no breaking changes to production runtime. Adapter templates implement the recommended call patterns (idempotent tool-calls, structured output via JSON schema). The contract tests are intentionally permissive for early iteration but flag shape regressions.

How to try locally: clone repo, cd quickstart/bridge-playground, cp .env.example .env, docker compose up --build, open http://localhost:5173 for the dev UI. The playground includes a small seed dataset and a sample query flow demonstrating prefix cache reuse and a tool call that fetches user metadata.

Related work: follows patterns from ENG-1773 (RAG adapter spec) and DOC-54 (authoring snippets). This implements a lighter-weight authoring flow compared to the full RAG studio; intended as a low-friction on-ramp for partner integrations.

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the docs wording around auth (we provide two modes: API-key passthrough for dev and mutual-TLS example for enterprise). The contract tests are in tests/bridge-contracts and should be easy to extend. CI includes a cached vector seed step to keep runtime under 4m on GitHub Actions.

review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Can we reduce the size of the seed dataset in CI to keep the action under 4m? I pushed a suggestion for a smaller CSV.
Maya Patel: Good call — switched to a 500-row seed and added caching in the workflow. CI run passed afterward.
Lina Gomez: Docs nit — in the auth section the mutual-TLS example didn't mention cert rotation. Suggest adding a short note.
Maya Patel: Added a short subsection on cert rotation and example command to rotate a dev cert.
Ravi Shankar: Contract tests are failing intermittently on CI due to timing; recommended adding retry/backoff in the test harness.
Maya Patel: Added a simple retry decorator and adjusted timeouts; reran and green.
Lina Gomez: Approved after docs clarifications.
Ethan Brooks: Approved; CI green. Ready to merge.
